name: Spinor
summary: Represents an angle or square spinor belonging to an external particle or an auxiliary reference.

syntaxes.description: represents a massless external spinor of chirality "Angle" or "Square".
represents a massive spinor with its little-group index implicit.
makes the "Upper" or "Lower" little-group index explicit.
represents an auxiliary reference spinor; its label need not be an external particle.

details: A spinor is an endpoint of a [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain). Use the string "Angle" for a ket written |i> and "Square" for a ket written |i]. When that spinor is the first endpoint of a chain, HEPCAT displays the corresponding bra automatically. You do not need a separate symbol for a bra.

The first argument tells HEPCAT what the spinor represents. "Helicity" denotes a massless particle. "Spin" denotes a massive particle with little-group spin indices. "Xi" denotes a reference spinor, such as one used to write a photon polarization.
The integer particle label refers to the particle's position in your ordered process. Thus, leg 3 is the third particle in that list; it is not a particle name, a helicity, or a spin index.

In Spinor["Spin", "Upper", "Angle", 1, j], the label 1 identifies the external particle and j identifies its little-group component. [MakeIndicesExplicit](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MakeIndicesExplicit) inserts such indices into an expression. [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) instead selects a physical spin projection.

An Xi label identifies a reference, not necessarily an external leg with that number. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can choose and substitute reference spinors for a complete diagram or channel calculation.

detail_sections.title: Momentum and crossing conventions
paragraphs: Analytic HEPCAT expressions use all external momenta incoming. To convert selected external momenta to the physical outgoing convention, apply [ReverseMomentum](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReverseMomentum) to the complete expression. Replacing particle labels alone does not supply the angle-spinor signs required by crossing.

name: SpinorChain
summary: Represents a spinor bracket or an ordered spinor chain with momentum insertions.

syntaxes.description: represents a bracket with two spinor endpoints.
represents a momentum chain with its given order.

details: The first and last arguments are [Spinor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Spinor) objects. The intervening arguments, when present, are momentum insertions written with [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom). For example, a square endpoint on leg 1, `Mom[2]`, and an angle endpoint on leg 3 display as [123>.

The endpoint types and number of momentum insertions determine the chain's chirality. Keep the momentum arguments in their intended order: p2 p3 and p3 p2 are matrix products, and their difference is controlled by spinor identities rather than ordinary commutativity.

In the typeset display, the middle labels give the momentum insertions in order. For example, [1234] is a square chain with p2 followed by p3. Parentheses group a summed momentum into one slot and commas separate multi-digit labels. The typed expression retains the endpoint chirality, momenta and spin indices.

Constructing a chain records the expression; it does not request every available simplification. Use [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) for algebraic reduction, or [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) and [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity) when you want to choose and record individual identity steps.

detail_sections.title: Momentum sums inside a chain
paragraphs: `Mom[Multiparticle[2, 3]]` records p2+p3 in one slot. It represents the same linear momentum insertion as `Mom[2]+Mom[3]`. The reducer can distribute such a slot when doing so is useful, while preserving the order of the remaining insertions.

A chain containing a composite momentum is not by itself an instruction to put that momentum on shell. Diagram-specific internal-shell information is supplied separately through [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes).

name: SpinorTrace
summary: Represents an ordered chiral trace of momentum matrices.

syntaxes.description: represents a momentum-matrix trace.

details: Each argument is a momentum insertion written with [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom). `SpinorTrace[Mom[1], Mom[2]]` is the two-momentum chiral trace; HEPCAT's reduction convention gives `2 MomProd[1, 2]`. It is not the four-component Dirac trace with an extra factor of two.

Longer traces retain the order of their momentum matrices. Apply [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) to use the supported trace and Clifford identities, or [ExtractEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractEnergy) to evaluate supported traces in explicit components.
Trace manipulations follow the same external on-shell convention as spinor chains. An internal propagator is not put on shell merely because its momentum appears in a trace.

examples.description: Reduce a two-momentum chiral trace to a scalar momentum product.
Display an ordered four-momentum trace.

name: Mom
summary: Represents a momentum in a spinor chain or a propagator.

syntaxes.description: denotes the four-momentum of particle i.

details: Mom[i] denotes the momentum of particle i in the ordered external-particle list. Place it between the endpoints of a [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain) to represent a momentum matrix, or inside [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) to identify the momentum carried by a propagator.

Mom[Multiparticle[1, 3]] denotes p1+p3. The [Multiparticle](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Multiparticle) head preserves the list of constituent legs so diagram, channel, and crossing functions can interpret the sum correctly.

To write a Lorentz scalar product, use `MomProd[i, j]`, with particle labels as arguments. See [MomProd](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProd) for scalar products. `Mom[i] Mom[j]` is ordinary multiplication of symbolic expressions and does not mean the scalar product.

An external label carries the usual external mass identity. A sum of momenta is generally off shell; diagram-local assumptions must be supplied by the diagram's mass rules when using [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes).

examples.description: Insert p2 between a square spinor on leg 1 and an angle spinor on leg 3. This represents [1|p2|3>, without evaluating a numerical momentum.

name: Mass
summary: Represents an external-particle mass or the assigned mass of an internal channel.

syntaxes.description: denotes the on-shell mass assigned to external particle i.

details: Mass[i] is the kinematic mass placeholder for external leg i. It is distinct from a model parameter such as the electron mass: the model's replacement list connects the placeholder to the appropriate parameter.
Mass[Multiparticle[1, 3]] labels the mass assigned to the channel carrying p1+p3. A diagram may therefore contain both external mass replacements and a replacement for this channel mass.

The replacement Mass[Multiparticle[1, 3]] -> m does not, on its own, assert that every occurrence of p1+p3 has invariant mass m. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) uses the declared channel information only within the permitted numerator scope. It keeps the actual [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) off shell.

Use [ParticleMass](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ParticleMass) to ask a model for a particle's mass, and [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) when you need the model's numerical parameter values.

examples.description: Compare the external mass label for particle 1 with the channel-mass label for p1+p3. They are separate placeholders even when a particular model assigns them the same parameter.

name: Multiparticle
summary: Labels the sum of a specified set of external momenta.

syntaxes.description: identifies the sum p_i1+p_i2+... as a typed channel label.

details: Multiparticle[1, 3] is a channel label. Inside [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom) it means p1+p3; inside [Mass](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mass) it identifies the mass assigned to that channel. The labels always refer to positions in the external-particle list.

This typed label lets [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams), [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels), and the amplitude checker recognize a channel without guessing which ordinary integer sums denote momenta.

Keep the typed label in stored amplitudes and mass rules. For algebra inside a chain, [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) can distribute a composite momentum into its individual insertions when useful. A composite label does not impose an internal on-shell condition.

summary: Represents a complex-deformed momentum insertion.

name: En
summary: Labels the energy of an external particle in explicit spinor formulas.

syntaxes.description: denotes the energy of external particle i.

details: En[i] denotes the energy of external leg i in the explicit component basis used by [ExtractEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractEnergy).
The spatial momentum convention is p {Sin[theta] Cos[phi], Sin[theta] Sin[phi], Cos[theta]}. These labels keep the particle number visible until you substitute a numerical or symbolic configuration.

For example, replace En[1] -> Sqrt[p^2+m^2] when evaluating a chosen configuration. Supply consistent energy, momentum magnitude, external mass and angles; assigning one coordinate does not generate or enforce momentum conservation.

name: SpinorEps
summary: Represents the antisymmetric tensor used to raise and lower massive little-group indices.

syntaxes.description: represents the antisymmetric little-group tensor with the given index variance.

details: The variance argument is "Upper" or "Lower". The other two arguments are little-group index labels, not external-particle labels. These tensors arise when explicit massive spinor indices are contracted.

For ordinary amplitude calculations, start with implicit massive spinors and use [MakeIndicesExplicit](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MakeIndicesExplicit) or [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) as needed. Apply [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) to sew the supported repeated indices rather than replacing their signs by hand.

Little-group index contraction and permutation of identical external particles are different operations. Symmetrizing the indices of one massive particle is handled by [SymmetrizeSpin](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SymmetrizeSpin).

name: Mandelstahm
summary: Represents the two-particle invariant (p_i+p_j)^2.

syntaxes.description: denotes the invariant (p_i+p_j)^2.

details: Mandelstahm[i, j] is HEPCAT's historical spelling of a Mandelstam invariant. It denotes the invariant itself, not the massive propagator denominator: the latter is Mandelstahm[i, j]-m^2.

Use [ExtractMandelstahm](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractMandelstahm) to convert supported [MomProd](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProd) and [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) expressions to this notation. Supply the multiplicity when working beyond four particles, since complementary two-particle invariants coincide only in the four-point case.

External momenta are all incoming. Crossing a leg therefore changes the momentum combination represented by an invariant; apply [ReverseMomentum](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReverseMomentum) to the typed amplitude before interpreting its physical scattering channels.

name: PropDen
summary: Represents a physical propagator denominator without putting its momentum on shell.

syntaxes.description: represents p_channel^2-m^2.
represents p_channel^2-m^2+I m width.

details: PropDen[Mom[Multiparticle[1, 3]], m] represents (p1+p3)^2-m^2. In an amplitude, divide by this object. The momentum and mass remain explicit, allowing [PhysicalPoleResidue](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PhysicalPoleResidue) and [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) to identify the corresponding physical pole.

The typeset display writes the square of a sum of external momenta as s with the channel labels in its subscript. For example, s123 denotes (p1+p2+p3)^2, and the denominator displays as s123 minus the propagator mass squared. A zero propagator mass leaves just s123. A supplied width contributes its usual imaginary term. Copying the typeset propagator recovers the typed PropDen expression.

The three-argument form adds the width term +I m width. Keep this sign convention when comparing with external numerical code. A package or library using another width convention needs an explicit conversion rather than an unannounced sign change.

Modern reduction and identity functions treat the arguments of PropDen as protected. Diagram-local internal on-shell identities can simplify a numerator, but must never replace the diagram's own denominator by zero.

[ExtractMandelstahm](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractMandelstahm) can rewrite supported two-particle denominators in invariant notation. This is an algebraic change of representation, not a residue evaluation or an internal-shell assumption.

name: MomProd
summary: Represents the Lorentz scalar product of two external or composite momenta.

syntaxes.description: represents p_i.p_j.
expands the scalar product over a momentum sum.

details: MomProd[i, j] means p_i dot p_j. Its arguments are particle or channel labels, without [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom) wrappers. For example, MomProd[Multiparticle[1, 2], 3] denotes (p1+p2) dot p3.
The displayed scalar product keeps its `MomProd` meaning when copied or read back from a notebook, so it remains usable by the symbolic and numerical tools.

Supported signed and composite arguments are handled bilinearly, and the scalar product is symmetric. For a single external leg, MomProd[i, i] becomes `Mass[i]^2` using its external on-shell identity.

MomProd[1, 3] does not automatically know which internal channel belongs to a particular diagram. If that diagram declares (p1+p3)^2=m_channel^2, [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can use `2 MomProd[1,3]=m_channel^2-Mass[1]^2-Mass[3]^2` in the diagram's numerator.

[ExtractMandelstahm](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractMandelstahm) expresses supported scalar products in terms of s invariants. Keeping MomProd in a numerator is also valid and can make later spinor reductions easier.

name: ApplyToNumerator
summary: Applies replacement rules to each existing additive term's numerator while preserving its denominator.

syntaxes.description: applies one replacement rule or a list of rules to each term's numerator.

details: Use this when an identity is allowed in a diagram numerator but must not act on its propagator. The function visits the additive terms already present in the expression and applies your replacement rule or rule list to each numerator.

It does not call Together or Expand first. A factored sum inside one term therefore stays within that numerator; separate rational terms are not merged into a common fraction before applying the rules.
Only the stated replacement is requested. The denominator of each visited term is restored unchanged, although ordinary Mathematica evaluation can simplify the resulting expression afterward.

This function does not decide whether your rules are valid identities or which internal channel is on shell. For a general diagram-preparation calculation, [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) obtains those assumptions from the item's declared mass rules and protects [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) factors.

name: ReduceSpinContractions
summary: Contracts repeated spin indices and joins the associated spinor factors into momentum chains.

syntaxes.description: applies supported spin-sum and little-group contraction identities.

details: Use this after sewing lower-point amplitudes or forming products that contain contracted massive or massless spinors. The function applies the supported spin sums and little-group epsilon contractions, replacing those index contractions by shorter typed spinor chains.

This is the usual first algebraic step for a diagram amplitude. The result may still contain several momentum insertions and reducible brackets; follow it with [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) for ordinary spinor identities.

The function does not choose reference spinors, generate factorization channels, or impose a diagram's internal-shell conditions. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) coordinates those preparation steps using the model and each item's declared mass rules.

A repeated spin index has a mathematical contraction meaning. Keep external spin indices distinct until you intend to sum them, or choose a definite component with [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex).

name: ReduceSpinorProducts
summary: Simplifies spinor chains, traces and products using ordinary identities and external-particle on-shell conditions.

syntaxes.description: returns a reduced expression using bounded, directed algebraic passes.

details: Use ReduceSpinorProducts when you already have a spinor expression and want routine algebraic simplification. It handles supported chain reversals, momentum-slot linearity, Clifford contractions, external Dirac equations, and product identities while comparing useful factored and expanded forms.

The input and output are ordinary HEPCAT expressions. A repeated external momentum inside a chain can become an external mass squared; an external momentum next to its own massless endpoint can make the chain vanish. Model-specific mass values can be substituted with ordinary replacement rules.

Ordinary Dirac and Schouten identities can simplify a sum even when a momentum chain has a trailing momentum word. The reducer also compares a contraction using both external endpoint equations, retaining its scalar-product term. Both angle and square chains, unequal masses and explicit massive spin indices use the same identities. These bounded passes do not assume that an internal line is on shell.

The function does not need a model or a complete process, so it cannot infer total momentum conservation from a list of external legs. For diagram or factorization preparation with that information available, use [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes).

detail_sections.title: Which on-shell conditions are used?
paragraphs: Only the external-particle identities belong to this process-independent reducer. It does not infer that a composite internal momentum has the propagating particle's mass. Those additional numerator assumptions are local to a diagram or selected factorization channel and are supplied separately by [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes).

The reducer protects [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) arguments, so simplifying a numerator does not also put the corresponding denominator on shell. The same ordinary reduction can therefore be applied to a completed, combined amplitude.

detail_sections.title: Choosing a form and following the calculation
paragraphs: There may be many equivalent forms with different numbers of terms and momentum insertions. The reducer uses finite, directed passes and bounded expansion. It aims to improve a practical complexity measure; it cannot promise the globally shortest possible formula.

The additional sum contractions are directional: the complete candidate must have a lower complexity score, or the same score with fewer expression leaves. Inverse spinor factors and propagator denominators remain protected. Positive powers are handled using their literal multiplicity, so taking one factor out of a square does not remove both copies. A distribution budget skips a large sum before expanding it.

If a useful identity is not chosen automatically, inspect [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) and apply a selected edit with [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity). Keeping that edit and its before/after expressions gives a derivation you can inspect and replay. [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) provides a consistent score for comparing intermediate forms.

name: SimplifySpinorProducts
summary: Runs the earlier iterative simplifier with explicitly declared external momenta and optional internal-channel information.

syntaxes.description: runs a directed iterative simplification with declared momenta and mass rules.

details: This function is retained for calculations built around HEPCAT's earlier three- and four-point simplification workflow. Unlike [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts), it is supplied a list of external momenta and can use its implemented momentum-conservation rules.

For a new general diagram calculation, prefer [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes). That function keeps process information and diagram-local assumptions with their amplitudes, chooses references, and reports preparation progress. For algebra without a process or model, use [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts).

The option names here are symbols, such as Momenta, InternalLines, InternalLineOnShell, nTimes, massReplacementRules and PrintWarnings. The newer preparation and identity functions instead use string option names. Copy the syntax of the function you are actually calling.

Defaults assume Momenta->{1,2,3,4}, InternalLines->{1,2}, InternalLineOnShell->False and nTimes->10. Change the external list when it does not describe your process. InternalLineOnShell->True permits additional channel assumptions and must be confined to that individual diagram.
The function can print the momentum-conservation and channel assumptions it uses. Inspect those assumptions before suppressing the messages with PrintWarnings->False.

name: ExtractMandelstahm
summary: Rewrites supported scalar momentum products and two-particle propagators in terms of s invariants.

syntaxes.description: uses the historical four-point convention.
uses n-point kinematics, applying complementary-pair identifications only when n is 4.

details: This is useful when you want to display a result in conventional channel invariants or compare it with a formula written that way. For distinct labels i and j, the conversion uses `2 MomProd[i,j]=Mandelstahm[i,j]-Mass[i]^2-Mass[j]^2`.

The one-argument form assumes four-point kinematics. At four points it also identifies complementary invariants, such as s34=s12. For a five- or six-point expression, supply the actual multiplicity as the second argument to avoid those four-point identifications.

A supported [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen)[Mom[Multiparticle[i,j]],m] becomes [Mandelstahm](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mandelstahm)[i,j]-m^2. Its pole is retained. The conversion does not set s_ij to an internal mass squared.

This representation is not always the easiest one to simplify further. [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) and [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can work with momentum products left in their typed form.

examples.description: Convert one scalar product without four-point pair identifications.

name: ReducexFactors
summary: Reduces the supported legacy four-point x-factor formulas for an explicitly specified channel.

syntaxes.description: applies the supported xFactorReduced and xTildeFactorReduced rules.

details: An x-factor is the three-point massless-vector building block carried in older constructive expressions. This routine combines the supported formulas using the external momenta and channel information you supply.

Its defaults are Momenta->{1,2,3,4}, ChannelMomenta->{1,4}, and ChannelMass->Mchannel. These describe a particular four-point channel. They must be changed when that is not the channel in your expression.

This is a specialized four-point routine, not a general expansion of every possible multi-particle x-factor. For current diagram calculations, [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) handles reference choices in the context of the actual process.
When comparing two completed amplitudes, do not use a channel-specific x-factor reduction as an unrestricted off-shell identity. Keep its chosen channel assumptions with the calculation.

name: ReduceColor
summary: Reduces contracted SU(3) color tensors and ordered generator traces.

syntaxes.description: reduces generator contractions, structure constants and traces in the canonical SU(3) representation.
also supplies a dimension for a dummy index whose tensor context does not determine it.

details: Use this with [ColorGenerator](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorGenerator), [ColorStructure](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorStructure), [ColorDelta](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorDelta) and [ColorTrace](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorTrace), the same color objects used by constructive diagrams and the Feynman comparison. There is one color representation for both workflows.

The normalization is `Tr(T^a T^b)=delta(a,b)/2` with three fundamental colors. Structure constants are real and satisfy `[T^a,T^b]=I f(a,b,c) T^c`. Thus `f(a,b,c)=-2 I (Tr(T^a T^b T^c)-Tr(T^a T^c T^b))`. An extra factor of I supplied by a vertex remains a separate coefficient.

Generator loops of any length become ordered traces. The SU(3) completeness identity contracts a repeated adjoint dummy between generators or traces. Hermitian conjugation swaps a generator's two fundamental slots, while conjugating a trace reverses its order. This also lets [SquareAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SquareAmplitude) form the correct conjugate color expression.

A repeated symbolic dummy label is summed, but an external [ColorIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ColorIndex) remains a free external color label by default. Literal positive integer indices are fixed matrix components, not dummy summation labels. A dummy used more than twice in one term is an invalid Einstein contraction and is reported explicitly.

Use `"SumExternalColors" -> True` on a squared or interfered color expression to sum its external ColorIndex slots explicitly. Each summed slot must occur twice. Dimensions are inferred from generator, trace and structure-constant slots; a pure delta loop may need `"IndexDimensions"`. This sum does not include an incoming-color average or a phase-space symmetry factor.

Generator, structure-constant and trace slots determine dummy dimensions automatically. A bare `ColorDelta[i,i]` cannot distinguish a fundamental loop from an adjoint loop, so it remains unresolved unless its dimension is supplied with `"IndexDimensions" -> {i -> 3}` or `{i -> 8}`. Generated internal indices already carry this information.

The optional `"MaxTerms"` limit defaults to 4096 and bounds color-polynomial expansion. An unsupported contraction or exceeded budget must not be interpreted as a numerical color certificate. Only SU(3) fundamental and adjoint identities are implemented.

name: SchoutenRewrite
summary: Rewrites a product of two spinor chains using a chosen generalized Schouten identity.

syntaxes.description: returns an equivalent two-product expression when the split chiralities agree.

details: Supply two chains and the split positions {m,n}. Each number counts the momentum insertions before the split in its chain: zero means next to the first endpoint, and the full insertion count means next to the last endpoint.

For chains without momentum insertions, {0,0} gives the familiar two-component Schouten relation between products of angle brackets or products of square brackets. With longer chains, the split determines which matrix strings accompany the recombined endpoints.

The result is an expression equal to the product of the original two chains. To use it inside a larger amplitude, replace that product there. [SchoutenCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SchoutenCandidates) finds eligible locations and packages the corresponding edits for you.

The split chiralities must agree. Invalid chains, incompatible chiralities, and out-of-range positions return $Failed. This identity does not need momentum conservation or an internal on-shell condition, and it may increase the displayed number of terms.

examples.description: Construct the ordinary angle-bracket Schouten identity.

name: SchoutenCandidates
summary: Finds the generalized Schouten replacements that can be applied to products of chains in an expression.

syntaxes.description: returns edit associations for eligible pairs of chains and splits.

details: Use this when a cancellation seems to require rearranging spinor pairings but you do not want to choose the chain pair and split positions by hand. The function searches the supported products and returns a list of edit associations.

Each edit records Name, Subtract, Insert, Chains and Splits. Its local algebraic action replaces the Subtract expression by Insert at the selected location. These records let you inspect both the identity and the chains to which it applies.

The list is a list of possibilities, not a simplification ranking. A valid Schouten move can initially make the expression longer. Compare the resulting whole expression, including cancellations with its other terms, rather than the inserted piece alone.

For a wider set of legal identities and application-time validation, use [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) together with [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity). Schouten generation itself uses no internal-shell assumption.

examples.description: Inspect the available Schouten identities.
Verify that a candidate records its replacement fields.

name: SpinorIdentityCandidates
summary: Lists the identity steps available for a spinor expression under its declared mass and momentum assumptions.

syntaxes.description: returns available exact edit associations.

details: The input is {massRules, expression}, the same two-part representation used for one diagram or one prepared amplitude. The result is a list of associations describing individual exact edits. It does not apply the entire list or automatically choose the best move.

Use the Name field to understand the kind of identity and inspect its Subtract and Insert expressions to see what changes. Apply a selected association using [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity); that function verifies that the edit is still legal for the current expression.

Chains are canonicalized and supported momentum sums are distributed before moves are enumerated. The displayed candidate list can therefore describe the normalized form of the input, rather than its original typesetting.

The candidate mechanism is useful for an explicit derivation: keep the input, selected edit, and output at each step. For an automatic preparation workflow with progress reporting, start with [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) instead.

examples.description: List identities without internal-shell or conservation assumptions.
examples.input: SpinorIdentityCandidates[{{}, SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 1], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 2]] SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 3], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 4]]}, "OnShellChannels" -> {}, "MomentumConservation" -> False]

detail_sections.title: Choosing the allowed assumptions
paragraphs: The string option "OnShellChannels"->Automatic uses only the internal channels declared by the supplied mass rules. This is appropriate while working on that particular diagram or selected channel. For a completed sum whose internal momenta must remain off shell, use "OnShellChannels"->{}.

The string option "MomentumConservation" defaults to True and uses the external-leg information available in the state. Set it to False if you are studying an isolated algebraic expression without the corresponding conserved process.

Use the same settings when applying a candidate. An identity generated with one set of channel assumptions must not be replayed as if it were valid with a different set. Physical [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) factors remain protected in either mode.

name: ApplySpinorIdentity
summary: Applies one validated identity step to a spinor expression.

syntaxes.description: validates and applies an edit returned by SpinorIdentityCandidates.

details: First obtain a candidate from [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) for the current {massRules, expression} pair. Pass that association as the second argument, using the same "OnShellChannels" and "MomentumConservation" options.

The result is the new expression, not a new pair. Retain the mass rules yourself when making the next state: {massRules, newExpression}. Keeping the rule list explicit makes it clear which diagram-local assumptions each step was allowed to use.

The function checks the candidate against the current legal moves. A stale candidate from an earlier expression, an incompatible assumption set, or an invalid edit produces $Failed and a message rather than silently changing the formula.

A legal move need not make the expression shorter. To explore a route, record Before, After, and the candidate association. [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) can help compare forms, while a sequence of recorded identities provides the actual algebraic justification.

examples.description: Select the available Schouten edit and apply it to the same starting expression. No internal-shell or momentum-conservation assumption is used.
examples.input:
state = {{},
  SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 1], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 2]]
  SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 3], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 4]]};
edits = SpinorIdentityCandidates[state,
  "OnShellChannels" -> {}, "MomentumConservation" -> False];
ApplySpinorIdentity[state, First[edits],
  "OnShellChannels" -> {}, "MomentumConservation" -> False]

name: SpinorExpressionComplexity
summary: Scores the size of a spinor expression, with extra weight for momentum insertions and scalar momentum products.

syntaxes.description: counts terms, momentum insertions and scalar momentum products with the package's simplification weights.

details: Use this to compare intermediate forms produced by [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts), [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes), or a manually chosen identity route. The score is the sum, over implicit monomials, of one plus four times the numerator momentum degree. This gives an explicit penalty to momentum factors, whether they occur inside or outside spinor chains.

Each chain or trace momentum insertion contributes one unit. [MomProd](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProd), [Mandelstahm](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mandelstahm) and a squared momentum contribute two units. Positive powers count every factor, so a scalar product squared contributes four units. A single insertion therefore scores 5, while one scalar product scores 9, the same as two insertions. Mass factors carry no momentum cost.

The score accounts for branches hidden in composite momentum slots. `Mom[Multiparticle[1,3]]` inside a chain represents two momentum contributions, so packing a sum into a single label does not make it artificially inexpensive.

Physical [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) factors and inverse kinematic factors are opaque to the numerator count. A momentum appearing only in a denominator does not count as a numerator insertion. The score measures a practical algebraic representation, not numerical stability, high-energy behavior, or whether the amplitude is physically correct. Use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) for those separate tests.

Two equivalent expressions can have different scores, and the lower-scoring intermediate form need not lie on the shortest route to the final answer. Retain useful alternative routes when a temporary increase exposes a later cancellation.

name: ComplicateAmplitude
summary: Generates an equivalent expression by applying a random sequence of reversible identity steps.

syntaxes.description: applies up to n eligible random edits; n defaults to 5.

syntaxes.input: ComplicateAmplitude[{massRules, expr}, n, RandomSeed -> seed, "RecordSteps" -> True]
syntaxes.description: records a reproducible trajectory.

details: This is useful for checking that a simplifier or a recorded derivation can recover an equivalent form. The input is {massRules, expression}; the second argument is the maximum number of random edits and defaults to 5.

The returned association contains "MassRules", "Original", "Expression", and "Steps". "Original" is the canonicalized starting expression, "Expression" is the last expression reached, and "Steps" is the number of moves actually made.

Set the string option "RecordSteps"->True to retain "Trajectory". Each trajectory entry contains "Before", "After", and "Candidate", so the random calculation can be inspected as an identity derivation rather than just compared at its endpoints.

An explicit integer RandomSeed makes the random choices repeatable. Automatic uses the ordinary random state within the routine's local random scope. The random path does not have to increase complexity at every step, and it can stop early when there are no eligible moves.

The "OnShellChannels" and "MomentumConservation" string options have the same scope as in [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates). For a completed amplitude, explicitly forbid internal-shell assumptions with "OnShellChannels"->{}.

examples.description: Generate and retain a short repeatable identity trajectory.
examples.input: ComplicateAmplitude[{{}, SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 1], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 2]] SpinorChain[Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 3], Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 4]]}, 2, RandomSeed -> 17, "RecordSteps" -> True, "OnShellChannels" -> {}, "MomentumConservation" -> False]

name: ReverseMomentum
summary: Crosses selected external momenta, including their spinor signs, in a complete amplitude expression.

syntaxes.description: reverses external momentum i.
crosses the listed legs in sequence.

details: HEPCAT derives analytic amplitudes with every external momentum incoming. If the numerical scattering process treats legs 3, 4 and 5 as outgoing, ReverseMomentum[expression, {3,4,5}] converts the supported typed momentum and spinor occurrences for those legs.

In HEPCAT's convention the angle spinor of a crossed leg changes sign while its square spinor does not. Explicit momentum insertions also change sign. The function counts every affected occurrence, including repeated insertions in a chain, and transforms composite momentum sums inside chains and propagators.
Apply crossing to the complete expression, including its denominators. A label permutation is a different operation and is handled by [PermuteParticles](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PermuteParticles).

When exporting a physical incoming -> outgoing process through [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess), supply the analytic all-incoming expression. The exporter performs this conversion itself. Pre-crossing that expression and asking the exporter to cross it again would count the signs twice.

Cross the momentum inserted on leg 2 in [1|p2|3>, without crossing either endpoint.

name: PermuteParticles
summary: Cyclically relabels selected external particles in typed spinor and momentum expressions.

syntaxes.description: maps i1 to i2, i2 to i3, and the last label back to i1.

details: The list {1,3,4} means 1 goes to 3, 3 goes to 4, and 4 goes to 1. Labels not in the list retain their values. Use a two-element list to interchange two legs.

The function changes supported particle labels in spinors, momenta, masses, momentum products, scalar invariants and x-factors. A little-group spin index is not a particle number and is left intact. Use this typed relabeling rather than replacing every integer in an expression.

A relabeling does not reverse a momentum and does not by itself supply the statistics sign required when comparing amplitudes under exchange of identical fermions. Apply [ReverseMomentum](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReverseMomentum) for crossing, and keep the process's Bose or Fermi exchange convention explicit when testing a physical symmetry.

When relabeling a whole diagram or process, keep its particle list, external mass assignments, channel rules and expression consistent. An expression with newly numbered legs must be compared against the correspondingly numbered process.

name: ReverseSequence
summary: Reverses a sequence of arguments for use inside another expression.

syntaxes.description: returns the arguments in reverse sequence order.

details: Unlike Reverse[{a,b,c}], this helper removes the intermediate List wrapper. Its result is intended to splice into the arguments of another head.
For general Mathematica list manipulation, prefer Reverse; this helper is useful when constructing a reversed spinor-chain argument sequence.

name: ChooseSpinIndex
summary: Selects one physical spin projection of a massive external particle.

syntaxes.description: inserts the explicit spin-index combination for particle i.

details: The particle argument identifies the external leg. The last argument is its physical spin projection, such as +1/2 or -1/2 for a fermion, or +1, 0 and -1 for a spin-one particle.

The input should contain that particle's implicit massive [Spinor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Spinor) factors. HEPCAT replaces them by the appropriate explicit little-group components. For the longitudinal spin-one state it uses the normalized sum of the two mixed index assignments.
This selects a state; it does not sum over states or average incoming spins. It also differs from merely naming indices with [MakeIndicesExplicit](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MakeIndicesExplicit).

The generated [SPINAS](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SPINAS) interface uses doubled-spin integers, while this symbolic function uses physical half-integer values. Thus a positive spin-half state is selected here by 1/2, not by the C++ label 1. To select several legs in particle order, use [ChooseSpinIndices](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndices).

examples.description: Choose the positive spin-half state of leg 1.
Choose the longitudinal state of a spin-one leg.

name: ChooseSpinIndices
summary: Selects physical spin projections for successive massive external particles.

syntaxes.description: applies ChooseSpinIndex to legs 1,2,... with the corresponding projections.

details: The projection arguments correspond to external legs 1, 2, and so on. The function applies [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) in that order, using the physical projections rather than doubled-spin C++ labels.

Use this when the desired spin configuration is most naturally written in external-particle order. To select only one particular leg, call [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) directly so the intended particle number is explicit.

The resulting expression is one selected spin configuration. Summing or averaging the squared amplitudes over a set of configurations remains a separate operation; [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) supplies that numerical interface for complete exported processes.

examples.description: Choose spin-half projections for both massive endpoints.

name: MakeIndicesExplicit
summary: Inserts specified upper little-group indices into the implicit massive spinors of an expression.

syntaxes.description: assigns the listed indices to particle i.
assigns the per-particle list at position i to particle i.

details: Use this when deriving a spin sum or when you need to see which massive-spinor occurrence carries which little-group index. For one spin-half leg, supply one index; higher-spin states need the corresponding list of two, three or four indices.
The two-argument form takes a list of index lists in external-particle order. An empty list can be used for a scalar leg. The three-argument form acts on one explicitly numbered particle.

Index insertion does not symmetrize the state or select a normalized physical projection. Use [SymmetrizeSpin](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SymmetrizeSpin) for index symmetrization and [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) for a definite physical spin state.

The implementation expands the relevant products while matching implicit factors. Internal spin contractions should be handled with [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) before assigning the remaining external indices.

examples.description: Insert one explicit upper little-group index.
Supply index lists in particle order.

name: MakeIndicesImplicit
summary: Removes the supported explicit upper massive-spin indices from spinor chains.

syntaxes.description: replaces explicit upper-index massive Spinor occurrences with their implicit form.

details: This restores the compact external-state notation after an explicit-index calculation. The supported upper-index [Spinor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Spinor) factors are replaced by the corresponding massive spinors with their indices omitted.

Omitting an index does not perform a sum over it and does not undo a physical spin projection. If the index was needed to distinguish components, preserve the explicit expression before suppressing that information.

For the opposite operation, use [MakeIndicesExplicit](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MakeIndicesExplicit). To sew repeated indices by a spin-sum identity, use [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions).

examples.description: Remove an uncontracted upper index.

name: SymmetrizeSpin
summary: Assigns and symmetrizes the little-group indices of one massive external particle.

syntaxes.description: averages the distinct index permutations for particle i.

details: Supply the leg number and a list of one through four index labels. The function inserts those labels into the particle's implicit massive spinors and averages over their distinct permutations.

Repeated labels have the correct permutation normalization: {i,i} has one distinct assignment, rather than two separately counted copies. This matters when spin-one and higher-spin expressions contain coinciding spin indices.

This is the symmetry of the spinor indices belonging to a single massive particle. It is not Bose or Fermi exchange of two external particles. Use [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) when you want a normalized physical projection such as the spin-one longitudinal state.

To supply index lists in external-particle order for several legs, use [SymmetrizeSpins](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SymmetrizeSpins). The unsymmetrized insertion operation is [MakeIndicesExplicit](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MakeIndicesExplicit).

examples.description: Symmetrize a pair of massive spin indices.
Keep a repeated index with unit permutation weight.

name: SymmetrizeSpins
summary: Symmetrizes massive little-group indices for a list of external particles.

syntaxes.description: applies SymmetrizeSpin to each particle's index list.

details: The index list at position i belongs to external leg i. For example, {{i},{j,k},{}} describes one spin-half leg, one spin-one leg, and one scalar leg.
The function applies [SymmetrizeSpin](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SymmetrizeSpin) to each particle. It averages distinct assignments within each particle, including the proper treatment of repeated labels.

This does not sum over physical external spin configurations or symmetrize identical particles. Those operations have different normalization and statistics factors. [SquareAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SquareAmplitude) uses these little-group manipulations when constructing a symbolic conjugate product.

examples.description: Assign one index to each massive endpoint.

name: ExpandSummation
summary: Writes supported contracted massive-spin indices as explicit two-component sums.

syntaxes.description: writes eligible repeated symbolic indices as a two-component sum.

details: Use this when you want to inspect a contraction component by component. Eligible repeated symbolic little-group indices are expanded into the +1/2 and -1/2 components used by HEPCAT.
The input is expanded before the matching contraction patterns are applied. This can be useful for checking a small spin sum but can make a large expression much longer.

For routine sewing, [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) usually gives a more compact expression directly in spinor chains. [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) selects a physical state instead of expanding a repeated-index sum.

examples.description: Expand a repeated massive upper/lower index.

name: SquareAmplitude
summary: Constructs an amplitude times its Hermitian conjugate, retaining the massive-spin contractions to be reduced.

syntaxes.description: constructs the conjugate product using the per-particle spins.

details: Supply an expression with implicit external massive indices and a list of physical spin magnitudes in particle order. The supported values are 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2 and 2. Internal spin contractions should already have been reduced.

The function makes one copy's massive indices explicit, symmetrizes the corresponding indices in the other copy, conjugates the first, and multiplies the two. The result can still contain spin contractions; follow it with [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) and [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) as needed.
Scalar couplings are conjugated as part of the Hermitian conjugate. A symbolic coupling g is therefore not assumed real unless that property has been established separately.

No initial-state spin average, identical-particle phase-space divisor, or external color sum is inserted here. [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) provides explicit spin sums and the declared scattering normalization for numerical work. Complex-shifted external-state expressions are outside this helper's intended scope.

Canonical color tensors retain Hermitian conjugation. Internally contracted color labels in the conjugate amplitude receive independent dummy names, so their sums are not accidentally tied to the original copy. External ColorIndex labels are retained; use [ReduceColor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceColor) with `"SumExternalColors" -> True` when a squared-color sum is wanted.

name: ExtractEnergy
summary: Evaluates supported spinor expressions in an explicit energy, momentum-angle and spin basis.

syntaxes.description: substitutes momentum matrices and two-component spinors for the listed particles.
supplies known external on-shell masses for stable numerical evaluation.

details: Use this to inspect a bracket numerically or compare an identity at a chosen set of momenta. It replaces supported momentum matrices and spinor endpoints by two-component expressions and evaluates the resulting matrix products and traces.

The particle list tells HEPCAT which external labels to evaluate. An entry {i} handles a massless or scalar leg. A massive spin entry {i, spin, projection}, such as {1,1/2,1/2}, also chooses its physical spin component.

The result uses [En](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/En)[i], [MomMagnitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomMagnitude)[i], [Theta](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Theta)[i] and [Phi](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Phi)[i]. The spatial momentum is p {Sin[theta] Cos[phi], Sin[theta] Sin[phi], Cos[theta]}. Substitute a complete, consistent set of these values after constructing the expression.

The function evaluates the supplied configuration; it does not generate conserved phase space or repair inconsistent momenta. To compare complete scattering amplitudes at controlled kinematics, use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes).

examples.description: Evaluate an angle bracket in explicit massless components.
Evaluate a scalar momentum product.
Retain a tiny massive spinor component after machine energy and momentum have rounded to the same value. The result is nonzero because the mass is supplied independently.
examples.input:
energyExpression = ExtractEnergy[
  SpinorChain[Spinor["Spin", "Upper", "Angle", 1, 1/2],
    Spinor["Helicity", "Angle", 2]], {{1}, {2}},
  "MassRules" -> {Mass[1] -> 1/2000, Mass[2] -> 0}];
energyExpression /. {En[1] -> 10.^12, MomMagnitude[1] -> 10.^12,
  Theta[1] -> 0., Phi[1] -> 0., En[2] -> 1.,
  MomMagnitude[2] -> 1., Theta[2] -> 0., Phi[2] -> 0.}

detail_sections.title: Masses and highly boosted particles
paragraphs: Supply known external masses through the string option `"MassRules" -> {Mass[1] -> me, ...}`. For supported positive-energy, on-shell numerical input, HEPCAT can then evaluate the small spinor component sqrt(E-p) as Abs[m]/sqrt(E+p), avoiding subtraction of almost equal numbers.

The supplied mass is independent physical input. Once rounded energy and momentum values have become equal, their difference cannot recover a tiny mass. The numerical consistency checks protect the stable substitution but do not prove that tiny mass from rounded data.
Symbolic formulas, signed-energy inputs, and unsupported branches retain their corresponding expressions. Supplying external masses does not impose an internal propagator's mass shell.

name: ExtractEnergy1
summary: Substitutes one particle's momentum matrices and explicit four-vector components.

syntaxes.input: ExtractEnergy1[expr, i, energy, momentumMagnitude, theta, phi]
syntaxes.description: replaces supported momentum occurrences for particle i.

syntaxes.input: ExtractEnergy1[expr, i, energy, momentumMagnitude, theta, phi, mass]
syntaxes.description: also supplies the known external on-shell mass for stable numerical components.

details: This is the first stage of ExtractEnergy. Spinor endpoints remain symbolic until ExtractEnergy2 is applied.
The time-space metric is (+,-,-,-). Upper and lower four-vectors carry the corresponding spatial signs. Momentum-matrix placement follows the chain's current chirality.
For a finished numerical scalar, normally use ExtractEnergy rather than stopping after this intermediate stage.

The optional trailing mass is used only by the supported real positive-energy on-shell numerical route. Omitting it preserves the original formulas; negative-energy, complex and clearly off-shell inputs retain the original branch behavior.
When the mass is known, a small momentum-matrix diagonal is rationalized using the mass and transverse momentum rather than subtracting nearly equal energy and longitudinal momentum.

examples.description: Expose the explicit momentum matrix in a chain.

name: ExtractEnergy2
summary: Substitutes explicit two-component spinor rows and columns for one particle.

syntaxes.input: ExtractEnergy2[expr, i, energy, momentumMagnitude, theta, phi]
syntaxes.description: replaces supported helicity and indexed massive spinor endpoints on particle i.

syntaxes.input: ExtractEnergy2[expr, i, energy, momentumMagnitude, theta, phi, mass]
syntaxes.description: also supplies the known external on-shell mass for stable numerical components.

details: This is the second stage of ExtractEnergy. It uses sqrt(E+p) and sqrt(E-p) for massive components, and sqrt(2E) for massless helicity spinors. With a known on-shell mass and supported positive-energy numerical inputs, the small massive component uses abs(m)/sqrt(E+p).
Explicit massive index values are +1/2 or -1/2. Chirality, variance and endpoint position determine the correct row or column and signs.
The returned SpinorChain can still contain vectors. ExtractEnergy performs the final conversion to Dot and Tr.

The optional trailing mass is used only by the supported real positive-energy on-shell numerical route. Omitting it preserves the original formulas; negative-energy, complex and clearly off-shell inputs retain the original branch behavior.

details: This is an earlier high-energy expansion that expresses supported massive-spin states through helicity and auxiliary reference spinors. It is useful only within the expansion order and spin cases implemented by the routine.

This older routine uses energy, momentum magnitude, masses and auxiliary Zeta spinors. The source describes it as implemented only to linear order, so do not treat it as a universal exact massive-to-massless replacement.
Use [ChooseSpinIndex](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndex) and [ExtractEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExtractEnergy) for explicit physical spin components without relying on this expansion.

name: ConvertStringAmplitude
summary: Reads a compact spinor-bracket string and constructs a typed HEPCAT expression.

syntaxes.description: uses the per-particle mass list to distinguish massless and massive spinors.
also supplies mass rules for composite endpoint labels.

details: Use this when importing a formula written in the older compact bracket notation. The mass list is in particle order and tells the reader whether a leg should be represented by a massless helicity spinor or a massive spinor.

The result contains ordinary typed objects such as [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain), [Spinor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Spinor) and [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom), so it can be passed to the algebra and preparation functions.

The optional symbolic option InternalMasses supplies mass information for supported composite endpoint labels. It is input information for interpreting the formula, not permission to put every internal line on shell.

For readable output use [PlainText](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PlainText). When storing a new exact amplitude in a model, use `PlainText[expression,"Model"]` or [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes) rather than relying on ambiguous handwritten compact strings.

summary: Marks supported momenta and spinors for a legacy complex deformation.

details: Use this at the symbolic marking stage of an earlier complex-shift derivation. It changes the supported ordinary spinor and momentum heads into their shifted counterparts, leaving the actual supported shift expansion to [ExpandComplexMomenta](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExpandComplexMomenta).
This is a symbolic marking step, not a complete general complex shift. [ExpandComplexMomenta](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ExpandComplexMomenta) implements the supported continuation cases.
The two-leg form distinguishes scalar products with one or both deformed momenta. Do not assume that arbitrary reference or mixed hatted objects have been transformed.

name: UnhatMomenta
summary: Removes the standard complex-deformation markers.

syntaxes.description: replaces SpinorHat, MomHat and MomProdHat12 by Spinor, Mom and MomProd.

details: Use this when a derivation has reached the stage at which its complex-deformation labels should be removed. It replaces the standard [SpinorHat](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorHat), [MomHat](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomHat) and [MomProdHat12](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProdHat12) heads by their ordinary counterparts.

This is a head replacement, not an evaluation of a shift parameter. It does not automatically remove the one-slot [MomProdHat1](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProdHat1) or [MomProdHat2](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomProdHat2) markers.
Use it only when the mathematical operation being performed justifies returning those objects to their unshifted form.

name: ExpandComplexMomenta
summary: Expands supported legacy complex-shift formulas with specified masses and companion legs.

syntaxes.input: ExpandComplexMomenta[expr, {i, mi}, k, {j, mj}, l, mik]
syntaxes.description: applies the implemented shift identities for the chosen mass pattern.

details: Use this to expand one of the particular massive or massless deformation cases implemented by the earlier shift machinery. The shifted particle pairs, their masses, companion legs and channel mass are mathematical input to that chosen construction.
The pair arguments identify the shifted legs and their masses; k and l identify the companion legs used by the construction, and mik is the corresponding channel mass.
This is a collection of specialized massive/massless cases. It is not a generic solver for an arbitrary complex deformation. Preserve the original expression and verify the assumptions when using it.
For an expression without any matching shifted object, the input remains unchanged.

name: ReplaceSpinorZ
summary: Replaces a two-index auxiliary z object in a supported massive shift.

syntaxes.description: rewrites SpinorZ["Both",I,J] when both specified masses are nonzero.

details: This helper belongs to the supported massive complex-shift calculation. It replaces the two-index auxiliary object associated with the specified massive legs and companion leg; it is not a general identity for arbitrary reference spinors.
The result is a sum of a massive spinor bracket and a chain with `Mom[k]`, divided by mi mj. The original upper/lower little-group indices are retained.
If either mass is zero, this particular replacement is not applied. It is not a generic rule for all SpinorZ forms.

name: SPINAS
summary: Converts supported chains and algebra to the earlier SPINAS C++ expression notation.

syntaxes.description: returns a C++ expression using the older named-product convention.

details: This expression formatter is retained for older scripts that assemble their own C++ process files. It returns text referring to named spinor products; it does not by itself construct those objects, assign momenta, compile code, or supply a complete spin sum.

For a new numerical process, prefer [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess). That function writes a complete class with product initialization, momentum updates, crossing, parameter handling, normalization and optional independent validation.

Do not interpret a successfully formatted string as a numerical or physical validation. The supported syntax is narrower than that of the complete exporter, and the earlier formatter does not provide all of its safeguards.

name: PlainText
summary: Converts a spinor expression to readable bracket text or exact model-file syntax.

syntaxes.description: returns compact human-readable text.
returns explicit text suitable for storing a supported exact expression in a HEPCAT model.

details: PlainText[expression] returns a string using compact angle and square brackets. It is useful for a plain-text derivation, a message, or a quick inspection of a formula outside the notebook display.

PlainText[expression,"Model"] has a different purpose: it writes a supported exact expression so the model reader can recover its meaning. It inserts explicit multiplication and typed forms wherever compact bracket notation would be ambiguous.

Model mode refuses unsupported or inexact objects with Failure. Use exact rational coefficients and symbolic model parameters when saving a reusable analytic amplitude; machine decimal approximations may have already discarded information.

To append a known amplitude to a factorization model, use [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes), which also checks the model entry. To generate a complete numerical C++ project, use [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess). PlainText by itself only returns text and writes no files.

name: ExpandMomHatAlt
summary: Expands supported all-line-shift momentum and propagator markers.

syntaxes.description: rewrites shifted composite propagators and chain momentum insertions.

details: This is the expansion step for the supported all-line-shift momentum markers. It rewrites the recognized shifted propagators and chain insertions, using the conventions of the earlier deformation code.

A [MomHat](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/MomHat) insertion in a chain becomes [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom) plus z MomQ. A shifted composite propagator is expressed using its unshifted [PropDen](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PropDen) and the channel roots zPlus and zMinus.
This legacy all-line-shift helper uses the package symbol ConstructiveDiagrams`z. It does not determine the auxiliary q momenta or solve for the roots.
Preserve the shift definitions and assumptions alongside the result. This is separate from ordinary amplitude preparation.
